name: creditdash
description: Ticker in, credit-structure dashboard out: who a company owes, in what order, when it comes due, and whether cash flow covers it, from its SEC filings.
long_description: Reads a company's latest 10-K/10-Q (or a US GAAP 20-F and its 6-Ks) from SEC EDGAR, extracts the debt note into a checked instrument list, and models debt service, coverage, the capital stack and the cash waterfall. Ask Claude about a ticker and it answers from a compact snapshot; ask to see it and the full dashboard opens in the chat or your browser. Needs your name and email for the SEC's User-Agent rule; a DeepSeek API key adds the instrument list and the market read (without one you get SEC totals only). Money is in $ millions.

tools.name: credit_snapshot
tools.description: Build a company's dashboard from its latest SEC filings and return a compact summary: interest coverage, debt instruments, maturities, capital stack, market read.

tools.name: show_dashboard
tools.description: Show the full interactive dashboard in the chat, or open it in the browser.

tools.name: set_market_inputs
tools.description: Save bond yields, 5-year CDS, ratings, consensus or price that the filings don't have.

tools.name: list_dashboards
tools.description: List the dashboards built so far.

sec_user_agent.title: Your name and email (for the SEC)
sec_user_agent.description: The SEC requires every request to name a contact, e.g. "Jane Doe jane@example.com". It is sent only to sec.gov.

llm_api_key.title: DeepSeek API key (optional)
llm_api_key.description: Just the key (it starts with sk-), from platform.deepseek.com. It reads the debt note into an instrument list and writes the market read; without it you get SEC totals only. About $0.01-0.03 per new filing.

data_dir.title: Data folder
data_dir.description: Where dashboards (out/), market inputs (overrides/) and the SEC cache are kept.
